# Facet radial centers: an exact source interface and two remaining obstructions

This is a follow-on to the audited H-tied one-group outer-contact law.
It uses the actual full-rank homothetic envelope and common chart from
`candidate 696a6484b3fda438`
and the legitimate convex perspective tests from
`candidate 9a8570db7f0b3f01`.
It does not assert a mixed inverse-power centerpoint theorem or infer a
Gamma payment from a facet center chosen at a new location.

## 1. The ordinary radial theorem does apply to each genuine facet law

Fix a facet F of D with unit outer normal n, dimension m=d-1>=1, and
positive height h=h_D(n). On F the own projective denominator is the
positive affine function P_D(xi)=1+a_D.xi. The relevant ordinary density is

    q_F(xi)=h P_D(xi)^(-d) 1_F(xi).                    (1)

Its inverse d-th power is affine and positive on the convex support:
q_F^(-1/d)=h^(-1/d)P_D. Thus it belongs to the compact bounded inverse-
power class with beta=d=m+1, exactly the threshold of the proved radial
centering theorem. It has an existential ordinary center c_F in relint F
at which every containing face halfspace has mass at least

    Gamma_m nu_F(F),   Gamma_m=(m/(m+1))^m.            (2)

This invokes the self-contained radial convexity/fixed-point theorem in
`candidate faf22898d0dc8331`.
It does not replace m+1 by the weaker borderline exponent m of a variable
height numerator. Constancy of h on the facet is essential here.

For an actual outer-contact subset E_z of this facet, restriction of (1)
to E_z has the same ordinary property if E_z has positive intrinsic
m-volume. E_z is convex, since it is the rescaled face of K_z on the
supporting envelope plane. Its own radial center may depend on z.
No assertion that this center is c_F is justified for a proper subset.

## 2. A positive statement for the FULL source facets

At a source base, K_z=y(z)+ell(z)D and the genuine common affine chart is

    R(z,X)=ell(z)+a_D.(X-y(z))=ell(z)P_D(xi).

The pure weighted physical facet measure is h R^(-d)dS_X. Since physical
facet area scales by ell(z)^(d-1), its pullback is EXACTLY

    ell(z)^(-1) q_F(xi)dS_F(xi).                       (3)

Hence every full source facet has the SAME normalized pointed law.
Choose one radial center c_F for (1). The physical centers

    X_z=y(z)+ell(z)c_F                                (4)

are affine in z and lie in the interiors of their source facets. They
therefore respect every anchored source relation and keep the original
integer labels. The center selection is family-compatible on this
homothetic source subfamily, and (2) holds in every such facet with its
actual mass from (3). This is a genuine positive use of the radial theorem.
It does not include arbitrary nonhomothetic exterior contact subsets E_z.

## 3. Exact uniform-lift obstruction already inside the genuine chart

Let c=nu_F(F)>0. Formula (3) gives whole source-facet masses

    W_z=c/ell(z).                                     (5)

Suppose two source bases z_- and z_+ and their midpoint z_0 are present,
and ell_-!=ell_+ with ell_0=(ell_-+ell_+)/2. Then for EVERY finite positive
continuous dimension r,

    W_0^(1/r)
       <[W_-^(1/r)+W_+^(1/r)]/2.                     (6)

Indeed s -> s^(-1/r) is strictly convex for s>0. Thus no compatible family
of uniform convex r-dimensional fibers at the original labels can have
these exact weighted masses, even up to a common positive multiplier.
This obstruction uses the actual chart R=ell P_D and full homothetic
source facets, not the arbitrary base extension used in the older
`candidate b0296f8a3b0d3d48`.

The statement is conditional on such an actual nonconstant-scale source
relation being present. It is not a construction of a deepest source face
with those scales. Conversely, any proposed uniform lift valid for every
actual source configuration would have to prove that the relevant source
relations have constant ell, or change the masses/representation target.
The ordinary affine center compatibility in (4) does not fix (6).

## 4. The face convex-test law alone cannot supply Gamma_d

Here is an exact obstruction to one tempting final inference. It retains
a full uniform source facet, convex contained exterior face pieces, the
actual canonical simplex cap trace, and ALL nonnegative convex face tests.
It does NOT assert a whole lattice-compatible family with actual common
critical source caps; those additional conditions remain the missing input.

Take d=2 and let D be a triangle marked at its centroid. Its ordinary
projective parameter is a_D=0. Parametrize one facet by t in [0,1]. For
the three canonical through-centroid caps, each of weight 1/3, the empty
opposite cap and the two remaining cap traces give

    W(t)=(1_{t>=1/3}+1_{t<=2/3})/3.

Thus W=2/3 on the middle third and W=1/3 elsewhere, almost everywhere.
The full source-facet law is uniform, so it is already the simplest
threshold-beta=m+1 law of Section 1.

Let C=[0,1/6] union [5/6,1], J=[1/3,2/3], and
R=[1/6,1/3] union [2/3,5/6]. Put

    rho(t)=1+4 1_C(t),    B=2/5<Gamma_2=4/9.          (7)

The density consists of the full source facet plus four copies of each
convex end-sixth. For every nonnegative convex phi,

    int_0^1 phi(t)(W(t)-B)rho(t)dt <=0.               (8)

Proof. Hermite--Hadamard on J, symmetric spreading of two points about
1/2, and Jensen on the two end-sixths give

    int_J phi <= [phi(1/3)+phi(2/3)]/6
              <=[phi(1/12)+phi(11/12)]/6 <=int_C phi.

The left side of (8) is exactly

    (4/15)int_J phi -(5/15)int_C phi -(1/15)int_R phi
       <=-(1/15)(int_C phi+int_R phi)
       <=-(1/30)int_0^1 phi.                          (9)

The last inequality uses int_J phi<=int_C phi. Thus the counterexample
has a strict reserve against bounded additional positive response terms:
if 0<=r(t)<=1/150, then, since rho<=5,

    int phi(t)[W(t)-B+r(t)]rho(t)dt<=0.                (10)

All interval endpoints are null and may use either closed-cap convention.
A small positive buffer moves the two cap endpoints from 1/3 and 2/3;
(8) itself is stated for the exact limiting simplex trace above. No
unverified uniform-in-buffer claim is used.

Consequently normal-conditional convex order, full source-facet presence,
and bounded positive response corrections do not ALONE recover the
unweighted ordinary projective cap credit. The exact exterior footprint
compatibility and actual cap criticality must enter a further argument.
The ordinary radial center in this example is just 1/2; selecting it does
not remove the exterior density rho or change the weighted stress.

## 5. The remaining lattice interface, stated without promotion

Flattening an actual outer face preserves the original integer labels
and gives a genuine mixed convex face support. A pure positive inverse-
power density on each fiber has the ordinary center in Section 1. In
face dimension one, the ordinary mixed Helly argument also gives an
existential weighted center with depth at least total mass/(2 k) for any
positive measure on this actual convex support. Neither fact identifies
that center with the marked source graph, nor does it bound every
individual old cap's weighted face mass by the global beta.

The surface separator controls an omega-WEIGHTED AVERAGE of old cap face
captures. A radial or mixed centerpoint covering argument supplies a
large capture for at least ONE old cap. These are different statements:
without an additional control of the actual omega weights or a shared
source/face allocation, the latter cannot contradict the former. No
exchange of the maximum over caps with that fixed weighted average is
valid. Formula (9) is an exact small-dimensional test of this gap.

Thus the legitimate new conclusions are the sharp ordinary facet law,
the affine SOURCE-center family (4), and the genuine-chart mass obstruction
(6). A lattice-preserving payment involving all actual exterior footprints
and the same cap weights remains unproved.
